title: Common formally smooth extension of two stack versal rings
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where local means having a unique maximal ideal. Let $k$ be a finite extension of $R/\mathfrak m_R$ [def-weil-field]. Schemes and algebraic spaces are [def-pc-scheme, def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. An algebraic stack is a category fibred in groupoids with effective etale descent for objects and sheaf descent for isomorphisms, diagonal representable by algebraic spaces, and a smooth surjective scheme atlas. Representable means that every scheme-valued 2-base change is an algebraic space. Smoothness is tested on smooth scheme atlases by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Locally of finite type means that a smooth scheme atlas has locally finite type composite to the base [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $\mathcal X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be an algebraic stack locally of finite type and let $x:\operatorname{Spec}k\to\mathcal X$ be an $R$-point [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For an Artinian local $R$-algebra $A$ with specified residue field $k$, let $\mathcal F_x(A)$ be the groupoid of pairs $(\eta,\alpha)$ with $\eta\in\mathcal X(A)$ and $\alpha:\eta|_k\cong x$, with arrows respecting the marking. Artinian means descending chains of ideals stabilize; all maps between test algebras are local and induce the identity on their specified residue fields. Here a versal ring at $x$ means a complete Noetherian local $R$-algebra $C$ with residue field $k$, equipped with a marked formal object: objects $\eta_n\in\mathcal F_x(C/\mathfrak m_C^n)$, $n\geq1$, with coherent transition isomorphisms $\eta_{n+1}|_{C/\mathfrak m_C^n}\cong\eta_n$. For a test algebra $A$ and a local $R$-map $v:C\to A$ inducing the identity on $k$ (it kills some $\mathfrak m_C^n$), write $\eta_v\in\mathcal F_x(A)$ for the pullback of $\eta_n$ along the induced map $C/\mathfrak m_C^n\to A$. Versality means: for every surjection $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ of test algebras, every such $v:C\to A$, every $\zeta'\in\mathcal F_x(A')$ and every isomorphism $\zeta'|_A\cong\eta_v$ in $\mathcal F_x(A)$, there exist a local $R$-map $v':C\to A'$ lifting $v$ and an isomorphism $\zeta'\cong\eta_{v'}$ in $\mathcal F_x(A')$ restricting to the prescribed one. Let $C$ be a versal ring at $x$. Let $k_1$ be another finite extension of $R/\mathfrak m_R$, let $y:\operatorname{Spec}k_1\to\mathcal X$ be an $R$-point, and let $D$ be a versal ring at $y$ in the same sense, using residue field $k_1$. Let $l$ be a field with specified finite $R$-embeddings $k\hookrightarrow l$ and $k_1\hookrightarrow l$, and fix an isomorphism $x|_l\cong y|_l$. Then there exist a complete Noetherian local $R$-algebra $H$ with residue field $l$ and local $R$-maps $C\to H$ and $D\to H$ inducing the specified embeddings, both formally smooth for the $\mathfrak m_H$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic].

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-stack-versal-finite-residue-extension] twice, to $(C,x,k\hookrightarrow l)$ and $(D,y,k_1\hookrightarrow l)$. Obtain versal rings $C_l,D_l$ at $x_l,y_l$, complete Noetherian local with residue field $l$, and adically formally smooth local maps $C\to C_l$, $D\to D_l$ inducing the specified embeddings. Both applications have finite residue extension and the same Noetherian local base $R$.

Put $z=x_l$ and use the given isomorphism $x_l\cong y_l$ to regard the marked formal object over $D_l$ as one at $z$: compose each marking to $y_l$ with the inverse isomorphism to $z$. This gives an equivalence of the test groupoids and preserves the prescribed-isomorphism lifting property. The marked deformation groupoids form a predeformation category [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category]: transport along $A\to B$ is pullback along $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. The identity and composition constraints are those of the fibred category, restricted to marked objects, so they satisfy the stated unit and associativity axioms. Over $l$ the unique arrow between markings $\alpha,\beta$ is $\beta^{-1}\alpha$. The formal objects have the specified transition isomorphisms. Their evaluations at a test algebra agree with the current definition: transport from any higher level is identified with transport from the least positive $N$ with $\mathfrak m_A^N=0$ by those transitions and the composition constraints. Thus changing markings preserves versality with these evaluations. Also $l$ is finite over $R/\mathfrak m_R$, hence of finite type over $R$. Apply [lem-sfb-stack-minimal-versal-power-series] to these two versal objects. After interchanging their roles if necessary, write $E=C_l$, $H=D_l\cong E[[t_1,\ldots,t_r]]$, with the isomorphism inducing the identity on $l$. The opposite case is treated by interchanging $C,D$ as well.

Take the map $E\to H$ corresponding to the coefficient inclusion into $E[[t_1,\ldots,t_r]]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-local-ring], its maximal ideal consists of series with constant coefficient in $\mathfrak m_E$. Thus this inclusion is local and induces the identity on $l$. The ring $H$ is already complete Noetherian local, since it was one of the extended versal rings. No additional construction of a completed tensor product is needed.

Check adic formal smoothness of $E\to H$ from [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. Let $J^2=0$ in an $E$-algebra $T$, and $g:H\to T/J$ kill $\mathfrak m_H^N$. Choose lifts $b_i\in T$ of $g(t_i)$. Then $b_i^N\in J$, hence $b_i^{2N}=0$. The ideal $I=(b_1,\ldots,b_r)$ satisfies $I^{r(2N-1)+1}=0$, since every monomial of that degree contains an exponent at least $2N$. Thus $T$ is $I$-adically complete: its quotient system is eventually constant. Evaluate power series by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-adic-evaluation] using the given coefficient map $E\to T$ and the $b_i$. Reduction of this evaluation is $g$: in $T/J$, both maps have the same coefficients and variable images and are continuous from the variables-adic topology to the ideal generated by the $g(t_i)$. For $g$ this continuity follows by sending the $M$th power of the variables ideal into the $M$th power of their image ideal; every series in a sufficiently high power is killed since that power is contained in $\mathfrak m_H^N$. Evaluation uniqueness therefore applies. This solves the lifting problem. When $r=0$, the coefficient inclusion is the identity and is formally smooth directly.

proof.text: Use $H$ as the required common ring, with maps $C\to C_l=E\to H$ and $D\to D_l=H$ (or the interchanged choices). The second map is formally smooth by step 1. For the first composite, a test map $H\to T/J$ killing $\mathfrak m_H^N$ restricts to a test map $E\to T/J$ killing $\mathfrak m_E^N$, since $E\to H$ is local. Lift that restriction over $C$ by step 1. Any such lift sends $\mathfrak m_E^N$ into $J$, so it kills $\mathfrak m_E^{2N}$. Now regard $T$ as an $E$-algebra through this lift and use step 4 to lift the original map from $H$. This is exactly the required $C$-linear lift [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. Locality composes, and the maps on residues are the specified embeddings followed by the identity of $l$.

I read the Stacks sources: stacks-geometry 0DQV/0DQX/0DQY with proofs, formal-defos definition-CLambda, 06T5 with proof, 0DQF, and artin.tex predeformation-category construction and 07WX. New node finite-residue-extension is 0DQY over Spec R. It is true because algebraic stacks satisfy RS, it is self-contained, and inseparable l is allowed. New node minimal-versal-power-series is the pairwise consequence of 06T5(2)+(3) and is true. Its 'finite type over R' hypothesis reduces to Stacks' 'finite over Lambda' because Artinian local R-algebras with residue field l are R_p-algebras with R_p->l finite. Neither new node duplicates the field-lifting nodes (07XG/07XT), the versal-ring existence node or the complete-local smooth power-series node, and neither restates the item. Steps: (1) the residue-extension node applied twice. (2) The marking is transported along x_l = y_l; this forms a predeformation category with the evaluation matching the current least-N convention, and the comparison node gives D_l = C_l[[t]] or the reverse, identity on l, with the symmetric case handled. (3) The coefficient inclusion is local by power-series-local-ring. (4) The b_i have b_i^{2N}=0, so I is nilpotent and T is complete; evaluation gives a lift, and uniqueness in T/J recovers g. (5) Lifting over C then over E gives the composite, the elementary form of 07EF.
